events.name: Dormition of the Theotokos Festival (Ano Skotina)
events.blurb: Religious feast celebrating the Dormition of the Virgin Mary at the church in Ano Skotina, the historic village above the beach, with a traditional panigyri (festival) each year on 15 August.

events.name: Olympus Festival (Dion Ancient Theatre & Platamonas Castle)
events.when: annually throughout July, August and September
events.blurb: Long-running summer arts festival of music and theatre staged at the ancient theatre of Dion and at Platamonas Castle in Pieria, both a short drive from Skotina beach.

events.name: Prometheia Festival
events.when: annually in early July near the summer solstice; 2026 edition 2-5 July
events.blurb: Multi-day festival on Mount Olympus near Litochoro reviving the ancient Greek spirit, with torchlight processions, ceremonies, dance, music and discussions honouring the myth of Prometheus.

events.name: Olympus Marathon
events.when: annually in late June; 2026 edition on 27 June
events.blurb: International 44 km mountain running race on Mount Olympus, starting from the archaeological site of Dion and finishing in nearby Litochoro.

events.name: Olympus Mythical Trail
events.when: annually in early July; 2026 edition on 4 July
events.blurb: Demanding mountain ultra-trail race set on Mount Olympus, based around Litochoro, aimed at experienced endurance athletes.

events.name: Olympus Adrenaline & Nature Festival
events.blurb: Outdoor-activities festival across the Dion-Olympos area featuring hiking, climbing, cycling, gastronomic workshops and cultural and experiential programmes around Litochoro.

events.name: Revolution of Olympus Commemoration (Litochoro)
events.blurb: Litochoro commemorates the 1878 Revolution of Olympus with festive events including a parade, traditional dances and a race in the town park.

events.name: Olympus Festival at Platamon Castle
events.when: annually in summer (July-September); concerts and theatrical performances staged inside the medieval Platamon Castle, a short distance south of the beach
events.blurb: Northern Greece's major music-and-theatre festival stages a series of summer concerts, ancient and modern theatre, and dance performances within the floodlit medieval Platamon Castle near the beach.

events.name: Feast of Saint Panteleimon (Panigiri)
events.when: annually on 27 July (with vespers the evening before); the village of Panteleimonas is named after the saint and marks the day with a church liturgy and a traditional panigiri with food, music and dancing
events.blurb: The community of Panteleimonas honours its patron, the great-martyr and healer Saint Panteleimon, with a Divine Liturgy followed by a traditional Greek panigiri of feasting, live music and folk dancing.

events.name: International Cultural Festival 'FolkWay' (South Pieria / Olympus Riviera)
events.when: annually in summer in the Leptokarya-Platamonas area of South Pieria; folklore dance and music groups from many countries perform over several days
events.blurb: An international folklore festival held in the South Pieria / Olympus Riviera area around Leptokarya and Platamonas, bringing together dance and music ensembles from around the world under the auspices of the regional unit of Pieria.

events.name: Panagia Anafonitria Monastery Feast (Dormition of the Virgin Mary)
events.when: annually on 15 August (the monastery also holds celebrations around 23 August); 2026 edition 15 August
events.blurb: Religious panigiri at the 15th-century Byzantine Monastery of Panagia Anafonitria, just inland from Navagio beach, honouring the Dormition of the Virgin Mary with liturgy, hymns and traditional gathering. The monastery is linked to Zakynthos patron Saint Dionysios.

events.name: Agia Paraskevi Festival (Volimes)
events.blurb: Village panigiri in Volimes (and Agios Leon) celebrating the feast of Agia Paraskevi, with religious ceremony followed by a lively fair of folk music, dancing and local food and wine.

events.name: Agios Dimitrios Feast (Volimes)
events.blurb: Religious festival in the village of Volimes celebrating the feast day of Agios Dimitrios (Saint Demetrius), one of the local panigiria of northern Zakynthos near Navagio beach.

events.name: Feast of Saint Dionysios (Patron Saint of Zakynthos)
events.when: annually on 24 August (main island celebration, with procession around 25 Aug) and again on 17 December; 2026 summer edition 24 August
events.blurb: The island's most important religious celebration honours its patron saint. The sacred relics of Saint Dionysios are carried in a grand procession through Zakynthos Town with psalms and the local philharmonic orchestra. The saint spent his last years at the nearby Anafonitria Monastery.

events.name: Zakynthos Carnival
events.when: annually in February–March, in the two weeks before Orthodox Lent (seven weeks before Greek Orthodox Easter)
events.blurb: A colourful two-week pre-Lenten carnival with Venetian-influenced Zakynthian traditions, including a town crier proclaiming the programme and a street procession with characters from Commedia dell'arte.

events.name: Milos Festival (Festival of Milos)
events.when: annually in July (typically a multi-day program of cultural events organised by the Municipality of Milos); some years extending into August
events.blurb: The island's premier summer cultural festival, with concerts, theatre, dance, art exhibitions and children's activities staged across Milos, including the village of Plaka and the ancient theatre of Klima.

events.name: Panagia Korfiatissa Panigyri (Feast of the island's patron saint)
events.when: annually in early May; week-long celebration centred in Plaka village with a religious procession
events.blurb: Religious festival honouring Panagia Korfiatissa, the patron of Milos, with an icon procession through Plaka plus traditional music and dance.

events.name: Feast of the Dormition of the Virgin Mary (Dekapentavgoustos)
events.when: annually on 15 August; celebrated at the Church of the Assumption in Adamas and with a major panigyri in the village of Zefyria
events.blurb: Greece's biggest summer religious feast, marked on Milos with church services and village panigyria featuring food, wine, music and dancing, including in Adamas near Sarakiniko.

events.name: Summer performances at the Ancient Theatre of Milos (Klima)
events.when: annually during the summer (July-August); occasional free musical and theatrical performances at the restored Hellenistic-Roman theatre
events.blurb: The restored ancient theatre at Klima/Tripiti hosts musical and theatrical evenings in summer, prized for its acoustics and sea views over the Aegean.

events.name: Milos Seafood Festival
events.when: annually in summer; held in the port town of Adamas (Adamantas)
events.blurb: A local food festival in the port of Adamas celebrating Milos's maritime heritage with fresh fish and seafood.

events.name: Plakias Festival
events.when: annually throughout August, nightly events in the town square and waterfront
events.blurb: A month-long summer festival in the seaside village of Plakias with nightly performances mixing traditional Cretan lyra and lute music, modern Greek pop, and international acts. Most events are free.

events.name: Feast of Agios Georgios (Saint George) in Plakias
events.blurb: Religious feast day celebrated in Plakias honouring Saint George, with church services and local festivities.

events.name: World Tourism Day Celebration in Plakias
events.blurb: Evening festival in the main square of Plakias with free street food, traditional Cretan music, songs and dancing performances to mark World Tourism Day.

events.name: Preveli Monastery Commemoration (Battle of Crete remembrance)
events.when: annually around the Battle of Crete anniversary (late May)
events.blurb: Commemoration at the Preveli Monastery, which sheltered Allied soldiers after the 1941 Battle of Crete. The Preveli International Memorial for Resistance and Peace honours Greek, Australian, New Zealand and British troops and Cretan civilians.

events.name: Kissamos Festival of Taste and Art (Festival Geuseon kai Technon)
events.when: annually in mid/late August; recent editions ran roughly 16-24 August on the seaside road west of the Kissamos Municipal Stadium
events.blurb: The Municipality of Kissamos's flagship annual festival celebrating local Cretan products, food, crafts and culture, with stalls, music and performances along the coastal road in Kissamos town, the nearest town to Balos Lagoon.

events.name: Vlatos Jazz Festival
events.when: annual summer series; 2026 edition runs every Sunday from 28 June to 27 September 2026 (14 candlelit acoustic concerts), concerts approx. 21:00-23:00
events.blurb: Intimate candlelit jazz, world music and Cretan-fusion concerts held inside the historic mountain church of Vlatos in the Kissamos region, southwest of Balos Lagoon. The 2026 season features tributes to Herbie Hancock, Bill Evans, Chick Corea and a Rebetiko night.

events.name: Anariza Fest
events.when: early-to-mid June (a short multi-evening series); 2026 edition closed on 13 June 2026 at 20:00
events.blurb: A West Crete arts festival on memory, identity and contemporary expression, blending traditional Cretan music with rock, jazz and electronic sounds. Held at the Ergo_stasio old woodcarving venue in Trachilos, about 1 km west of Kissamos Port, with live performances and the documentary 'Chronicles of Kissamos'.

events.name: Elos Chestnut Festival (Giorti Kastanou)
events.when: annually on the third Sunday of October, in Elos village, Innachorion area of the Kissamos municipality
events.blurb: A cherished autumn harvest festival in the chestnut-tree village of Elos in the Kissamos region. Visitors enjoy chestnut-based dishes, tsikoudia spirit, live music, traditional folk dancing and costumes. It is the best-known traditional festival near Kissamos, though Elos lies inland some distance from the Balos coast.

events.name: Kornaria Festival
events.when: annually from early July to mid-August; 2026 edition runs July-August (full program announced by the Municipality of Sitia in the weeks before July)
events.blurb: Eastern Crete's main summer arts festival, organised by the Municipality of Sitia. Concerts of Cretan and Greek music, dance, theatre, art and photography exhibitions, talks, and sports events including the Kornarios road race and beach volleyball. Main venue is the Venetian Kazarma fortress in Sitia, with additional events staged in surrounding villages such as Palekastro, the nearest town to Vai.

events.name: Panagia Festival (Dormition of the Virgin) at Palekastro
events.blurb: Religious panigiri held every 15 August in Palekastro (the nearest village to Vai) for the Dormition of the Virgin Mary, with a church service followed by a traditional feast of food, raki, live Cretan music and dancing into the night.

events.name: Holy Trinity / Carnival Festival at Palekastro
events.when: annually on the last Sunday of the Carnival season (late winter, before Lent)
events.blurb: A local Palekastro festival in honour of the Holy Trinity, organised each year on the final Sunday of Carnival with traditional Cretan music, dance and village festivities.

events.name: Metamorphosis tou Sotiros Festival at Zakros
events.blurb: Village panigiri for the Transfiguration of the Saviour held every 6 August in the Zakros area, southeast of Vai, featuring a church liturgy followed by a traditional feast with Cretan lyra music and dancing.

events.name: Barcarolle (Varkarola) Festival in Assos
events.when: annually on 24 August; 2026 edition expected 24 August 2026
events.blurb: Traditional Venetian-derived serenade festival held in the port of Assos, the closest village to Myrtos Beach. Local musicians sing folk songs from a decorated fishing boat surrounded by smaller boats and lit torches, followed by a fireworks display. Combined with the religious commemoration of Saint Cosmas of Aetolia, with a morning litany and icon procession.

events.name: Feast of the Dormition of the Virgin Mary in Assos
events.blurb: Assos holds a traditional celebration on the Dormition of the Virgin Mary, with a church service in honour of the Panagia followed by a local feast (panigiri) featuring traditional food, music and dancing in the village square.

events.name: Festival of the Olive and Olive Oil, Kastro (Pylaros)
events.when: annually in October during the olive harvest season
events.blurb: Annual gastronomy festival in the village of Kastro in the Pylaros area near Myrtos Beach, celebrating Kefalonia's olive-growing tradition with olive oil tasting and traditional production demonstrations.

events.name: Feast at the Monastery of Adeliko, Pylaros
events.blurb: A religious celebration and traditional feast held at the Monastery of Adeliko in the Pylaros region near Myrtos Beach, with food, music and dancing.

events.name: Panigiri of Panagia Tourliani (Dormition of the Virgin)
events.when: annually around 15 August (Dormition of the Theotokos), with celebrations continuing to the monastery's main feast on 23 August; held in Ano Mera village square
events.blurb: The most important religious panigiri on Mykonos, centred on the 16th-century Panagia Tourliani monastery in Ano Mera (~2.5 km from Ftelia). A procession, all-night feasting with traditional food, wine, music and dancing in the village square.

events.name: Panigiri of Agia Marina, Ano Mera
events.blurb: Traditional summer name-day feast held in Ano Mera, the inland village nearest to Ftelia beach, with local food, wine, music and dancing.

events.name: Mykonos Summer Festival
events.when: annually late June through August; open-air concerts, theatre, art exhibitions and film screenings around Mykonos Town
events.blurb: Island-wide summer cultural programme of open-air concerts, theatre, folk-music nights, art exhibitions and film screenings at venues such as the windmills and the Archaeological Museum courtyard in Mykonos Town (~6 km from Ftelia).

events.name: Mykonos Running Festival (Half Marathon, 10K, 5K)
events.when: annual road-running festival on Mykonos (recent editions held in September/October); routes start and finish in Mykonos Town
events.blurb: Annual running festival on Mykonos with half marathon, 10K and 5K races for all abilities, based around Mykonos Town within ~10 km of Ftelia beach.

events.name: XLSIOR Mykonos Festival
events.when: annually in late August; 2026 edition 20-25 August across various Mykonos beaches and venues
events.blurb: Large international summer music and party festival staged across Mykonos beaches, terraces and waterfront venues over several days in late August.

events.name: Mykonos Antanaclasis Festival
events.when: annually in September and October; series of classical, jazz and world-music concerts
events.blurb: Annual late-season concert series on Mykonos featuring world-class soloists performing classical, jazz and world music in island venues.

events.name: Dragano Honey Festival
events.blurb: Traditional honey festival in the village of Dragano (about 12 km from Egremni, between Komili and Athani), celebrating southwestern Lefkada's renowned honey. Visitors taste honeycombs, honey pie and pasteli, watch honey-harvesting demonstrations, and enjoy folk music and dancing.

events.name: Vasiliki Sea Feast
events.blurb: Maritime festival in the coastal village of Vasiliki (about 16 km from Egremni) celebrating the village's seafaring heritage with boat races, swimming competitions, fresh seafood, traditional dances by the sea and festivities lasting into the night.

events.name: Englouvi Lentil Festival (Feast of Agios Donatos)
events.blurb: Festival in the mountain village of Englouvi honouring Lefkada's famous local lentils, with free lentil soup, wine and sardines followed by live music and traditional dancing. Held elsewhere on the island, roughly 30 km from Egremni.

events.name: Lefkas International Folklore Festival (LIFF)
events.when: annually in late summer; the 2026 edition is scheduled for 26-30 September 2026 (held in Lefkada town)
events.blurb: Long-running international folk music and dance festival founded in 1962, bringing groups from many countries to Lefkada town (about 35-39 km from Egremni) for performances promoting peace and cultural exchange.

events.name: TRIMAN Triathlon
events.when: annually in spring; 2026 edition 8-10 May 2026 at Olympiaki Akti, Katerini
events.blurb: International triathlon (swim, bike, run) held right at Olympic Beach, with Mount Olympus and the Thermaic Gulf as the backdrop. Organised by the TRIAS triathlon club with support from the Pieria Tourism Organization.

events.name: Paralia Summer Fest (International Music & Dance Festival)
events.when: annually each summer (typically June-August); a 2026 edition runs 11-15 June 2026 in Paralia and Olympic Beach
events.blurb: International folk dance and music festival staged on the main squares and streets of Paralia and Olympic Beach, with folklore groups, choirs, orchestras and majorette teams performing traditional and modern dances. Several editions are held across the summer season.

events.name: International Cultural Festival 'Folkway' (Olympus Riviera, Central Pieria)
events.when: annually in summer (late June to late August depending on edition); held in the seaside towns of Paralia and Olympic Beach
events.blurb: Multi-day international cultural festival organised by the Municipality of Katerini together with Folkway/Open Ways, bringing folklore ensembles and cultural groups to the seaside resorts of Paralia and Olympic Beach on the Olympus Riviera.

events.name: Festival Days in Greece (Paralia Katerini)
events.when: annually in summer; a 2026 edition runs 8-12 July 2026 in Paralia, Katerini
events.blurb: International folklore festival of music and dance in Paralia Katerini, gathering ensembles, choirs and dance groups from various countries for non-competitive performances of traditional dances and songs.

events.name: Children and Youth Festival of Central Macedonia & Thessaly (S.Po.S.)
events.when: annually in late spring; the 15th edition was held on 30 May 2026 in Katerini
events.blurb: Regional children's and youth folk-dance festival in Katerini gathering hundreds of young dancers from groups across Central Macedonia and Thessaly.

events.name: Dragano Honey Festival (Giorti Meliou)
events.when: Annually in mid-August (typically around 12 August); village of Dragano, next to Athani
events.blurb: Festival in the village of Dragano (adjacent to Athani, just inland from Porto Katsiki) celebrating the region's renowned thyme honey, with honey tastings and exhibitions of local products alongside traditional music and folk dancing.

events.name: Assumption of the Virgin Mary Festival, Kalamitsi (Dekapentavgoustos)
events.when: Annually on 15 August; Kalamitsi village (southwest Lefkada)
events.blurb: One of Lefkada's most important panigiria, celebrated with particular grandeur in the southwest village of Kalamitsi. The day begins with a church service and is followed by a community feast of homemade dishes and local wine, with traditional music and dancing into the night.

events.name: Vasiliki International Sailing Regatta
events.when: Annually in summer (a Wildwind regatta week is scheduled around mid-September); Vasiliki bay, the nearest port to Porto Katsiki
events.blurb: An annual international sailing regatta held in the windsurfing and sailing hub of Vasiliki bay, the closest port to Porto Katsiki, drawing athletes and visitors to one of the Ionian's premier watersports venues.

events.name: Vasiliki Watersports Festival
events.when: Annually each summer; Vasiliki and Ai Gianni beaches
events.blurb: A summer watersports festival in Vasiliki, world-famous for its afternoon thermal winds, featuring windsurfing and sailing activities that draw hundreds of athletes and thousands of spectators to the bay.

events.name: International Festival "Paralia and Leptokarya Fest"
events.when: annually late August to early September; 2025 edition 29 August - 3 September
events.blurb: International folklore festival hosted partly in Leptokarya, bringing together folk and modern dance ensembles, choirs, majorette teams and orchestras from many countries for performances of songs, dances, music and traditional costumes.

events.name: International Cultural Festival "FOLKWAY" (Olympus Riviera / South Pieria)
events.when: annually in summer (typically late June to early September), staged across Leptokarya and Platamonas
events.blurb: International cultural and folklore festival of the Olympus Riviera / South Pieria, with editions held in the seaside towns of Leptokarya and Platamonas, featuring folk dance, choral and orchestral groups from around the world.

events.name: Olympus Festival (Festival Olympou)
events.when: annually July to end of August
events.blurb: Major annual arts festival of the Pieria region running since 1972, with ancient and modern theatre, dance, music and visual arts by Greek and international artists. Performances are staged at historic venues including the Castle of Platamon, a short distance up the coast from Leptokarya.

events.name: Platamon Castle Summer Concerts
events.when: annually during summer (July-August), as part of the Olympus Festival
events.blurb: Open-air summer concerts and theatrical performances staged inside the Byzantine Platamon Castle, just up the coast from Leptokarya, forming part of the regional Olympus Festival programme.

events.name: Bourtzi Cultural Events (Summer Festival)
events.when: annually every July and August, open-air theatre at the Bourtzi peninsula and Skiathos cultural centre
events.blurb: Municipality of Skiathos summer cultural programme at the Bourtzi open-air theatre, featuring concerts, theatrical performances, dance shows, art exhibitions and Karagiozis shadow theatre.

events.name: Feast of Agia Paraskevi
events.blurb: Traditional religious feast (panigiri) on Skiathos honouring Agia Paraskevi, with folk dances, traditional music and local costumes.

events.name: Dormition of the Virgin Mary Feast (Dekapentavgoustos)
events.blurb: Major Greek Orthodox feast celebrated across Skiathos with church services, festive gatherings and traditional celebrations honouring the Dormition of the Virgin Mary.

events.name: Papadiamantis Days
events.blurb: Annual literary and philological symposium in Skiathos dedicated to the island's famous writer Alexandros Papadiamantis, with narrations, musical evenings, exhibitions and walking routes.

events.name: Skiathos Fest (International Folk-Dance & Music Festival)
events.when: annually late June / early July; 2026 edition 28 June - 2 July
events.blurb: International folk-dance and music festival held in Skiathos, bringing together folklore dance and music groups for performances and cultural exchange.

events.name: Feast of Agios Ioannis Kleidonas
events.when: annually on 23-24 June (Midsummer / St John's celebration)
events.blurb: Traditional Midsummer celebration on Skiathos tied to the feast of St John, featuring the Kleidonas custom, bonfires and folk festivities.

events.name: Sardine Festival (Sardelas Day), Stomio
events.when: annually in late July (typically 26 July); coastal fishing-village celebration in Stomio
events.blurb: Gastronomy festival on the Stomio seafront celebrating the local fishing tradition, with free roasted sardines, cultural activities about fishing and live music. Co-organised by the Municipality of Agia and the Region of Thessaly.

events.name: Kissavos Marathon Race
events.when: annually in April, starting/finishing at the Central Square of Agia; 2026 edition 26 April
events.blurb: Mountain trail running event on Mount Kissavos (Ossa) above Agia, with several distances (around 40 km marathon, ~20 km trail and ~12 km path races) attracting hundreds of runners each spring.

events.name: Filoktiteia Cultural Festival
events.when: every summer (July-August) across the Municipality of Agia, with musical and theatrical events
events.blurb: Annual summer cultural festival organised by the Municipality of Agia, featuring musical and theatrical performances, alongside the 'With a View of the Sea' seafront events programme.

events.name: Chestnut Festival, Karitsa
events.when: annually in late October (e.g. weekend of 25-26 October) in Karitsa, on the slopes of Mount Ossa
events.blurb: Autumn harvest festival in Karitsa honouring the local chestnut crop, with traditional dances, a hike in the Kalypso Gorge, talks on chestnut cultivation, children's activities and free roasted chestnuts.

events.name: XLSIOR Festival Mykonos
events.when: annually in the second half of August; 2026 edition 20-25 August
events.blurb: One of the world's largest LGBTQ+ dance and party festivals, held across multiple Mykonos venues over roughly five to six days. Running since 2009, it draws tens of thousands of visitors to the island.

events.name: Panigiri of Panagia Tourliani (Feast of the Assumption)
events.blurb: Traditional religious feast honoring the patron saint of Mykonos at the Panagia Tourliani Monastery in Ano Mera village (about 8 km from Mykonos Town), with processions, services, music, dancing and communal food.

events.name: Mykonos Summer Festival
events.when: annually from late June through August
events.blurb: A month-long cultural celebration featuring open-air concerts, theater performances, art exhibitions and film screenings, held at iconic venues such as the windmills of Mykonos Town and the Archaeological Museum courtyard.

events.name: Greek Orthodox Easter (Epitaphios processions)
events.when: annually around Orthodox Easter (April); solemn candlelit Good Friday Epitaphios processions through Mykonos Town and villages
events.blurb: During Holy Week, candlelit Epitaphios processions wind through the alleys of Mykonos Town and the villages on Good Friday, with local bands and communities walking behind flower-adorned biers.

events.name: Feast of the Dormition Apodosis at Panagia Tourliani Monastery
events.when: annually on 23 August (the monastery's principal feast day)
events.blurb: The main feast day of the Panagia Tourliani Monastery in Ano Mera, marking the Apodosis (leave-taking) of the Dormition of the Theotokos, with religious services and traditional celebration.

events.name: Feast of Saints Barnabas and Bartholomew (Tragonisi)
events.blurb: A traditional feast held each year at the church of Panagia on the islet of Tragonisi off Mykonos, on the feast of Saints Barnabas and Bartholomew, with a religious service followed by communal celebration.

events.name: Kyrveia Festival
events.blurb: Ierapetra's main summer cultural festival, running from mid-July to the end of August with folk music and dance nights, concerts, theatre, handicraft exhibitions and beach parties, many held at the Kales fortress. Many events are free to the public.

events.name: International Documentary Festival of Ierapetra (IDFI)
events.blurb: An annual international documentary film festival held each August in Ierapetra, the southernmost town in Europe, screening competition documentaries from Greece and around the world. The 12th edition ran 2-22 August 2025.

events.name: Feast of Agia Foteini (Saint Photini)
events.when: annually in late February (26 February in the Greek tradition)
events.blurb: Agia Fotia beach takes its name from the small chapel of Agia Foteini (Saint Photini) beside it, whose Orthodox feast is commemorated on 26 February in the Greek tradition. Local chapels dedicated to the saint hold a liturgy on her name day.

events.name: Sinarades Panigiri (Nativity of the Virgin Mary)
events.blurb: The traditional village festival (panigiri) of Sinarades, the hilltop village just above Agios Gordios beach, celebrating the Nativity of the Virgin Mary with a church service followed by live music, Greek dancing, and food stalls (spit-roast lamb, souvlaki, loukoumades). Sinarades shares this feast date with nearby villages such as Afra and Marathia.

events.name: Corfu Orthodox Easter
events.when: 2026-04-12 (Orthodox Easter Sunday; Holy Week from early April)
events.blurb: Corfu is famous for its elaborate Orthodox Easter, including the Holy Saturday 'botides' pot-throwing in Corfu Town, Good Friday epitaph processions led by the island's philharmonic bands, and the midnight Resurrection service. It is the island's biggest annual celebration, observed across Corfu including the villages near Agios Gordios.

events.name: Litany (Procession) of Saint Spyridon, 11 August
events.blurb: One of the four annual litanies of Corfu's patron saint, Saint Spyridon, held in Corfu Town with the island's philharmonic bands (including the Sinarades Philharmonic, which serves the village above Agios Gordios) marching in the procession. The relics of the saint are carried through the streets.

events.name: Agia Marina Feast (Panigiri)
events.when: annually mid-July (St Marina's day, around 17 July)
events.blurb: Almyrida and the surrounding Apokoronas villages honour Saint Marina with a small panigiri around her feast day in mid-July, featuring traditional Cretan food, sweets, local wine and live music with dancing.

events.name: Feast of Agia Paraskevi, Kalyves
events.blurb: The nearest town of Kalyves celebrates its patron Saint Paraskevi on 26 July with a traditional church feast and panigiri including live Cretan music and local food.

events.name: Dormition of the Virgin Mary Panigiria (Apokoronas)
events.blurb: On 15 August, the Dormition of the Virgin Mary is the biggest religious celebration across Crete, with open-air panigiria, food, wine and traditional music in villages throughout the Apokoronas region around Almyrida.

events.name: Ifestia Festival
events.blurb: Annual festival launched from Oia that re-enacts Santorini's volcanic eruption with a large fireworks display (and in recent years a drone light show) over the caldera. Organized by local volunteers since 1991, it is free to watch from caldera viewpoints above Ammoudi.

events.name: Feast of Panagia Platsani (Dormition of the Virgin Mary)
events.when: annually on August 15 (procession on the eve, Aug 14)
events.blurb: The name day of the Panagia Platsani church on Oia's main square, celebrated on August 15 with religious ceremonies and a traditional panigiri (village feast). On the eve a procession carries the shroud of the Virgin Mary through Oia.

events.name: Greek Orthodox Easter in Oia
events.blurb: Oia marks Orthodox Easter with midnight church services, candlelit processions, fireworks and traditional feasts, one of the most important celebrations in the Greek calendar.

events.name: Festival of Prophet Amos (Profitis Amos panigiri)
events.blurb: Faliraki's traditional panigiri held at the Monastery of Prophet Amos for the prophet's feast day, with church services followed by local food, music, dancing and ouzo. The 19th-century monastery sits above the resort near Anthony Quinn Bay.

events.name: Festival of Traditional Rhodian Gastronomy (Roditiki Ladopitta)
events.blurb: An annual food festival in Faliraki celebrating traditional Rhodian cuisine, centered on the local olive-oil pastry 'Roditiki Ladopitta', with tastings of regional products.

argilos.town: Sitia (nearest beach settlement: Xerokampos), Lassithi, Crete

events.name: Kornaria Festival (Kornareia)
events.blurb: Sitia's flagship summer cultural festival honoring the Cretan Renaissance poet Vitsentzos Kornaros, with music concerts, theatre, traditional dance, art and photography exhibitions, lectures and sports events such as the 'Kornarios' road race and beach volleyball, held mainly at the Venetian fortress of Kazarma.

events.name: Sultanina Raisin Festival
events.blurb: A three-day festival in Sitia dedicated to the local sultanina grape variety, marking the start of the grape harvest with wine, traditional food, music and dance.

events.name: Dormition of the Virgin Mary panigiria (Dekapentavgoustos)
events.blurb: On 15 August villages across the Sitia and Lassithi area celebrate the Dormition of the Virgin Mary with church services followed by panigiria, featuring live Cretan music, traditional dishes and dancing in the village squares.

events.name: Carnival of Sitia (Apokries)
events.blurb: Sitia's popular carnival celebrations with a treasure hunt and a large costume parade on Carnival Sunday.

events.name: Evia Ultra Trail
events.blurb: A UTMB- and ITRA-certified mountain ultramarathon based in Steni Evias on Mount Dirfys, the nearest mountain town hub to Chiliadou Beach. The 2026 edition (held 4-5 April) features a 108.5 km ultra plus a two-runner relay, starting and finishing in Steni.

events.name: Steni Outdoor Fair (1 September)
events.blurb: A traditional outdoor commercial fair held in the mountain village of Steni Dirfios, where visitors can see, taste and buy local products from across Evia island.

events.name: Milos Festival
events.when: annually in summer, typically starting July
events.blurb: The island's main cultural event, organized by the Municipality of Milos, featuring concerts, theatre, dance, art exhibitions and film screenings staged at venues across the island. It traditionally begins in July and runs for several weeks.

events.name: Feast of the Dormition of the Virgin (Panigiri tis Panagias)
events.blurb: The most important religious festival on Milos, celebrated in Adamas and at the Church of Panagia Portiani in Zefyria with church services followed by a panigiri of traditional music, dancing, local food and wine.

events.name: Feast of Agios Sostis (Provata)
events.blurb: A saint's-day panigiri held in the village of Provata, the community closest to Firiplaka beach, with a church service and a traditional celebration of food, wine and folk dancing.

events.name: Feast of Panagia Korfiatissa (Plaka)
events.blurb: Celebration of Milos's patron icon at the Panagia Korfiatissa church in the capital Plaka, featuring a religious procession through the village along with folk music and dance.

events.name: Xerokampos Panigiri (feast of Agios Ioannis)
events.blurb: On 29 August the locals of Xerokampos, the nearest coastal settlement to Gerondolakkos beach, hold a traditional panigiri (religious feast) in honour of Saint John, with a church service followed by food, raki, live Cretan music and dancing.

events.name: Kornaria Festival
events.blurb: Sitia's main summer cultural festival, named after the 17th-century Cretan poet Vitsentzos Kornaros, fills the town with music, theatre, dance, exhibitions and sporting events such as the 'Cornarian' race and beach volleyball.

events.name: Sultanina (Raisin) Festival
events.blurb: A festival in Sitia dedicated to the local sultana grape variety, celebrating the area's traditional raisin production with food, wine and music.

gianiskari-beach.town: Akrotirio Araxou / Kato Achaia (West Achaea), with Patras as nearest city

events.name: Patras Carnival (Patrino Karnavali)
events.when: annually, late January to Clean Monday (2026: Jan 17 - Feb 23)
events.blurb: The largest carnival in Greece and one of the biggest in Europe, held in Patras (the regional capital about 45 km from the beach). The 2026 edition runs from January 17 to Clean Monday (February 23), with the grand parade of satirical floats around the carnival weekend and the ritual burning of the Carnival King effigy at the harbour to close it.

events.name: Kato Achaia Carnival & Clean Monday Kite-Flying (Koulouma)
events.when: annually during Carnival season, ending on Clean Monday (2026: Feb 23)
events.blurb: The town of Kato Achaia (seat of the West Achaea municipality, the nearest sizeable town) holds its own carnival parades, and on Clean Monday the koulouma custom is celebrated with families flying kites on the beach, marking the start of Lent.

events.name: International Festival of Patras
events.when: annually in summer (typically June to September)
events.blurb: A long-running summer cultural festival in the wider Patras / Achaea region featuring music, theatre and dance performances at venues including the ancient Roman Odeon. It is the main summer cultural program for the area around Araxos and Kato Achaia.

events.name: Nafplion Festival
events.blurb: Nafplio's prestigious classical and jazz music festival, held every summer since 1992 in historic venues such as the Bourtzi fortress and old-town squares. The 35th edition is scheduled for 11-18 July 2026.

events.name: Nafplio Carnival (Anapliotiko Carnival)
events.blurb: Nafplio's lively annual carnival with parades, satire, music and dancing through the old town, culminating in the traditional Koulouma celebration. The 2026 edition runs 15-23 February under the theme 'Global Upheaval'.

events.name: Nafplio Challenge (Nafplio Action)
events.blurb: Annual multi-sport event organised by the Municipality of Nafplio, featuring open-water swimming and running races in the Tolo area plus triathlon and aquathlon races, held each autumn in recent years.

events.name: Panagia (Assumption of the Virgin Mary) Festival, Palekastro
events.blurb: The village of Palekastro, the nearest settlement to Karoumes Beach, holds its annual panigiri for the Dormition of the Virgin Mary on 15 August, with traditional Cretan music, dance, food and drink.

events.name: Kornaria Festival, Sitia
events.blurb: Sitia's main cultural festival, dedicated to Cretan poet Vitsentzos Kornaros, runs for over a month with concerts, dance, theatre, art and photography exhibitions and sports events such as the Kornarios road race and beach volleyball, held mainly at the Venetian Kazarma fortress.

events.name: Mediterranean Festival of Sitia
events.blurb: A three-day festival at the port of Sitia blending Greek traditional music with contemporary sounds from the wider Mediterranean, Balkans and East, including exhibitions and workshops.

kedrodasos-beach.town: Paleochora (nearest town); Pelekanos / Chrissoskalitissa-Elafonissi area is closest to the beach

events.name: Panagia Chrissoskalitissa Monastery Panigiri (Dormition of the Virgin Mary)
events.blurb: On 15 August, the Dormition of the Virgin Mary, the clifftop Panagia Chrissoskalitissa Monastery just above Elafonissi (about 2 km from Kedrodasos Beach) holds one of western Crete's most popular panigiria, combining church services with a folk festival of traditional Cretan music, dance and food overlooking the Libyan Sea.

events.name: Agios Georgios Feast at Chrissoskalitissa Monastery
events.when: annually 23 April (or the Monday after Greek Easter)
events.blurb: A popular panigiri honoring Agios Georgios is held at the Monastery of Chrissoskalitissa, the landmark just above Elafonissi beach near Kedrodasos, on 23 April (or the Monday after Easter when the dates coincide).

events.name: Paleochora Music Festival (Summer Festival)
events.when: annually in the first ten days of August
events.blurb: The seaside town of Paleochora, the nearest town to Kedrodasos Beach, hosts a long summer festival in the first ten days of August featuring live music, traditional Cretan dance, puppet and classical performances, art exhibitions and local food and drink.

events.name: Kalitsounia (Cretan Cheese Pie) Festival, Kantanos
events.blurb: In the village of Kantanos in the hinterland above Paleochora, a kalitsounia festival celebrates the region's traditional herb- and cheese-stuffed Cretan pies with local food and music.

events.name: Dormition of the Virgin Panigiri at Adamas
events.blurb: On the feast of the Dormition of the Virgin (Kimisi tis Theotokou), a panigiri is held at the church of Agia Triada in Adamas, Milos's main town and the departure point for Kleftiko boat trips, with local music, dancing, food and Melian wine in the church courtyard.

events.name: Panigiri at Panagia Giatrissa
events.blurb: A traditional Greek panigiri at the historic chapel of Panagia Giatrissa on Milos, featuring folk music, local food and circle dancing.

events.name: Milos Festival
events.blurb: An annual cultural festival on Milos featuring Greek music, theater and dance performances, often staged in historic venues such as the island's ancient theater near Klima.

events.name: Panigiri of Panagia Korfiatissa, Plaka
events.blurb: A spiritual celebration honoring Milos's patron saint, centered on a religious procession through the village of Plaka where locals carry icons, accompanied by traditional music and local food.

events.name: Barbarossa Pirate Festival (Koursariko)
events.blurb: Naoussa's most famous celebration re-enacts the 1537 repulsion of the pirate Barbarossa, with masked locals staging a mock pirate raid in the harbour followed by fireworks, live music, dancing, and local treats such as octopus, small fish and souma. It traditionally takes place nine days after the Assumption of the Virgin.

events.name: Naoussa Fish and Wine Festival
events.when: annually on the first Sunday of July
events.blurb: Fishermen fry fresh fish on their boats in Naoussa harbour and offer it to visitors alongside local wine and souma, accompanied by traditional music and dancing. The festival was started by local fishermen in the 1970s.

events.name: Festival of Agios Ioannis Detis
events.blurb: One of the larger summer saint's-day panigiria (religious feasts) near Naoussa, celebrated with church services, food, music and dancing in the Agios Ioannis Detis area on the Monastiri peninsula north of the town.

events.name: Klidonas Festival
events.blurb: A traditional midsummer custom marking St John's Day, where Maytime wreaths are burned and revellers jump over bonfires; in the Naoussa area it is celebrated as part of the wider Parian Klidonas festivities with music and dancing.

events.name: Prophet Elias Festival (Panigiri) in Vivari
events.blurb: The seaside village of Vivari, the nearest settlement to Kondyli beach, holds its big traditional panigiri in honour of Prophet Elias every year on 20 July, with music, dancing and local food.

events.name: Nafplio Festival (Nafplion Festival)
events.when: annually in mid/late June to July
events.blurb: A long-running classical music festival held in nearby Nafplio (about 13-17 km from the beach), staging concerts in landmark venues such as the Vouleftikon and the courtyard of St George's church. It has run for over 30 consecutive years and is regarded as one of Greece's leading festivals of its kind.

events.name: Nafplio Marathon
events.blurb: An annual running event in nearby Nafplio that draws thousands of runners from Greece and abroad, with routes through the historic town and along the Argolic Gulf coast.

events.name: Nafplio Carnival
events.blurb: Nafplio's annual carnival features lively parades, elaborate costumes, traditional Greek music and dancing through the streets of the old town.

events.name: Feast of the Panagia & Varkarola (Kanaria Festival)
events.blurb: Parga's biggest annual celebration for the Dormition of the Virgin Mary. On the eve of 14 August people sail by boat to the islet of Panagia opposite the town for a folk festival, and on 15 August the Varkarola re-enacts the return of the Pargians from exile in Corfu, with two lines of Venetian-lamp-decorated boats crossing the bay and a fireworks display over the Venetian castle. The events center on Parga harbour and Kryoneri beach, where the Panagia islet church sits offshore.

events.name: Parga Summer Festival
events.blurb: A summer series of cultural events in Parga including concerts, art exhibitions and theatrical performances, often staged with the Venetian castle as a backdrop.

events.name: Orthodox Easter (Pascha) in Parga
events.blurb: Parga marks Orthodox Easter with solemn processions, midnight Resurrection mass and traditional feasting throughout the town.

events.name: Feast of Panagia Eikonistria (Kounistra)
events.blurb: Skiathos celebrates its patron saint, Panagia Eikonistria (Kounistra), each year on 21 November. The miraculous icon is carried in procession from Skiathos Town to the Kounistra Monastery, with worshippers keeping vigil around fires on the eve of the feast.

events.name: Skiathos Fest - International Folk-Dance & Music Festival
events.when: annually late June to early July (2026: 28 June - 2 July)
events.blurb: An international folk-dance and music festival held at the main square of Skiathos Town, gathering folk ensembles, choirs and dance teams from across Europe. The XII edition runs 28 June to 2 July 2026.

events.name: Bourtzi Cultural Festival ("Dream on the Wave")
events.blurb: The Bourtzi Cultural Centre on the small peninsula in Skiathos Town hosts a summer programme of theatre, concerts, art exhibitions and literary readings, named after Alexandros Papadiamantis's novel "Dream on the Wave."

events.name: Papadiamantis Days
events.blurb: A literary symposium honouring Skiathos-born author Alexandros Papadiamantis, with narrations, musical evenings, exhibitions and guided walks along paths the writer described in his works.

events.name: Feast of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary (Dekapentavgoustos) at Agia Triada, Adamas
events.blurb: On August 15 a major feast (panigiri) is held in the courtyard of the Agia Triada (Holy Trinity) church in Adamas, the town next to Langada Beach, with traditional music, dancing, food and local Melian wine. It is one of the most popular celebrations on Milos.

events.name: Milos Festival
events.when: annually in summer (roughly July to September)
events.blurb: The Festival of Milos is the island's main cultural event, running through the summer months with concerts, art and book exhibitions, dance, theatrical performances and activities for children at venues across the island, including Adamas, the town beside Langada Beach.

events.name: Holy Spirit feast at Agia Triada, Adamas
events.when: annually in June (moveable, 50 days after Orthodox Easter)
events.blurb: A moveable religious celebration of the Holy Spirit (Pentecost Monday) is held at the Agia Triada church in the centre of Adamas, near the port and Langada Beach.

events.name: Agia Marina panigiri
events.blurb: A traditional Milos panigiri honouring Saint Marina is held in mid-July at the chapels of Agia Marina, one of several summer village feasts on the island near Adamantas where visitors are treated to local food, wine, music and dancing.

events.name: Dekapentaugoustos panigiria (Feast of the Virgin Mary, August 15)
events.blurb: August 15 (the Dormition of the Virgin Mary) is one of the two main feast days on Chios, marked by panigiria across the southern Mastic villages near Emporios with church services, traditional food, music and dancing.

events.name: Feast of Agia Markella (St. Markella pilgrimage)
events.blurb: The largest religious celebration on Chios, held July 22 at the Monastery of Agia Markella near Volissos. Pilgrims travel from across the island and Greece, some walking the roughly 45 km from Chios Town, to honor the island's patron saint.

events.name: Chios Mastiha Festival
events.when: annually summer (kicks off in June, peaks in August)
events.blurb: A summer-long celebration of Chios mastic (mastiha), with cultural projects and events in Chios town, Kampos and the Mastic villages of southern Chios, tied to the traditional mastic harvest.

events.name: PelionFestival (International Classical Music Festival)
events.blurb: Annual classical music festival across East Pelion mountain villages, featuring concerts, masterclasses and lectures. The 2026 program runs July 18-31 with performances staged in villages including Tsagarada and Kissos, near Mylopotamos Beach.

events.name: Agia Marina Panigiri, Kissos
events.blurb: On the feast day of Saint Marina, the nearby village of Kissos holds a large panigiri in its flagstoned square by the 17th-century Agia Marina church, with traditional Greek music and dancing open to all.

events.name: Feast of Prophet Elias, Mouresi
events.blurb: Mouresi, the municipal village above Mylopotamos Beach, holds a traditional panigiri in the village square for the Feast of the Prophet Elias in July, with food, music and dancing.

events.name: Dekapentavgoustos Panigiria (Dormition of the Virgin)
events.blurb: On 15 August most Pelion villages, including those around Tsagarada and Mouresi, celebrate the Dormition of the Virgin with open-air panigiria featuring traditional music, dancing and local food.

events.name: Feast of Panagia Myrtidiotissa (Mirtiotissa Monastery)
events.blurb: The Holy Monastery of Panagia Myrtidiotissa, perched on the hillside just above Myrtiotissa Beach between Vatos and Pelekas, celebrates its patronal feast of the Virgin Mary Myrtidiotissa each 24 September with a liturgy and a traditional panigiri (festival) in nearby Vatos.

events.name: Pelekas Village Festival (Panagia Odigitria)
events.blurb: The village of Pelekas, the nearest hilltop settlement to Myrtiotissa Beach, holds its annual panigiri on 23 August in the square next to the church, with a morning liturgy followed by an evening of live Corfiot music, dancing and food.

events.name: Panagia Kastriani Festival (Dormition of the Virgin Mary)
events.blurb: The island's largest panigiri, held at the cliff-top Panagia Kastriani monastery about 7 km east of Otzias beach, honoring the patron Virgin of Kea with a procession, liturgy, live island music, dancing, wine and a communal meal of patatato.

events.name: Agia Marina Fair
events.blurb: A large summer fair on Kea dedicated to Agia Marina, one of the island's traditional patron-saint feasts celebrated in mid-summer with food, music and dancing.

events.name: Agia Triada (Holy Trinity Day) Feast
events.when: annually in June (Holy Trinity / Pentecost Monday)
events.blurb: A traditional celebration held in June at the seaside chapel of Agia Triada on Kea, featuring a feast where mules adorned with colorful rugs carry supplies up to the chapel.

events.name: Kea Fairy Tales Festival
events.blurb: An annual mid-summer storytelling festival on Kea where renowned Greek and foreign narrators read tales to children and adults.

events.name: Argalasti Olive Festival (Festival of the Olive)
events.blurb: Argalasti, the main village serving the Paltsi area, holds an annual Festival of the Olive in August celebrating the local olive harvest, alongside other cultural events including open-air theatre plays staged at nearby Korfos beach.

events.name: Agia Paraskevi Festival, Lafkos
events.blurb: The largest panigiri (saint's-day festival) in the nearby South Pelion village of Lafkos, marking the feast of Agia Paraskevi with church services and live traditional music and dancing in the village square.

events.name: Saint Athanasios Festival, Lafkos
events.blurb: A traditional panigiri in nearby Lafkos honouring Saint Athanasios, featuring a liturgy with artoklasia (the blessing and sharing of bread), communal food, dancing and celebrations.

events.name: Nativity of the Theotokos Festival, Lafkos
events.blurb: A South Pelion panigiri in Lafkos celebrating the Nativity of the Theotokos, with a church service followed by a large celebration in the town square featuring live traditional music and dancing.

events.name: Feast of Agios Ioannis (St. John) and the Klidonas custom
events.when: annually late June (around 24 June, St. John's feast)
events.blurb: The village of Agios Ioannis, immediately next to Papa Nero Beach, celebrates its patron saint with a religious feast (panigiri), during which the traditional Klidonas custom is revived. The celebration centers on the village chapel and includes food, music and dancing.

events.name: Zagora Apple Festival (Giorti Milou)
events.blurb: The town of Zagora, seat of the Zagora-Mouresi municipality that governs Agios Ioannis, holds an annual Apple Festival celebrating its renowned local apple production, with tastings, food, music and traditional dancing as part of the municipality's Cultural Summer events.

events.name: Panigiri of Agios Ioannis Prodromos (Vizitsa)
events.blurb: A large panigiri (saint's-day festival) for Agios Ioannis Prodromos is held in the Pelion village of Vizitsa on 29 August, featuring traditional food, wine, music and dancing well into the night.

events.name: Pelion / Zagora Cultural Summer (Politistiko Kalokairi)
events.blurb: The Municipality of Zagora-Mouresi runs a Cultural Summer programme of musical, theatrical and traditional events across its villages (including the Agios Ioannis area) throughout the summer season.

events.name: Thassos Dance Festival "Palataki"
events.blurb: A three-day traditional Greek dance festival held in Limenaria, named after the early-1900s "Palataki" monument building. It features live folk orchestras, dance presentations over two nights, historical guides and local cuisine, organised by the Cultural Research Centre and the Limenaria cultural association.

events.name: Sardine Festival, Skala Kallirachi
events.blurb: A summer seaside feast near Limenaria celebrating Thassos's fishing tradition with grilled sardines, local drinks, music and dancing along the coast.

events.name: August Fires (Avgoustiatika), Limenaria
events.blurb: A traditional community gathering in Limenaria and other Thassos villages on the night of 31 July, marking the transition into August with small fires, music, food and drinks.

events.name: Panagia (Dormition of the Virgin) Festival
events.blurb: One of the most significant religious celebrations on Thassos, marked across the island with a church procession, feasting and night-long dancing in the village squares of Panagia and Theologos.

events.name: Festival of Agios Epifanios (Saint Epiphanius)
events.blurb: Saint Epiphanius is the patron saint of Akrotiri, the village above Red Beach, and his blue-domed church sits along the road connecting the village to the beach. The feast features a liturgy, traditional foods such as fava beans, capers, sardines and olives, and an evening folk-dance festival with dance groups from across Greece.

events.name: Feast of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary (Dekapentavgoustos)
events.blurb: On 15 August the village of Akrotiri, the nearest settlement to Red Beach, holds one of Santorini's major panigiria for the Assumption of the Virgin Mary, with church services followed by live music, traditional dancing and communal feasting.

events.name: Feast of Agia Theodosia (Saint Theodosia)
events.blurb: The feast day of Agia Theodosia is celebrated at her church in Akrotiri village near Red Beach on 29 May, with religious services and local festivities for the community.

richtis-gorge.town: Sitia (nearest town to Richtis Gorge beach; closest villages are Exo Mouliana and Kalavros)

events.name: Kornaria Festival
events.blurb: Sitia's main annual cultural festival, named after the Cretan Renaissance poet Vitsentzos Kornaros, with concerts of music, dance and theatre, art and photography exhibitions, talks and sports events held at the Venetian Kazarma fortress and around town. It also incorporates village raki festivals (Kazanemata) and Klidonas celebrations.

events.name: Sultanina Raisin Festival
events.blurb: A multi-day festival in Sitia celebrating the local sultanina grape and the start of the grape harvest, featuring traditional Cretan music and dance in the main square plus sultanina-inspired dishes in local eateries.

events.name: Mediterranean Festival of Sitia
events.blurb: A three-day music festival in Sitia blending contemporary sounds with Greek and wider Mediterranean, Balkan and Eastern musical traditions, accompanied by exhibitions and creative workshops.

events.name: Feast of Agios Georgios (Saint George) in Plakias
events.blurb: Plakias hosts one of the larger panigiria (traditional religious feasts) in the Rethymno region on the feast day of Saint George, with a church service followed by live Cretan music, food and dancing in the village.

events.name: Dormition of the Virgin Mary panigiri (Dekapentavgoustos)
events.blurb: On 15 August, the Dormition of the Virgin Mary is the largest religious festival across Crete, and villages around Plakias and Lefkogia (which has a church dedicated to the Virgin Mary) hold panigiria with traditional music, food and dancing.

events.name: Maroneia-Sapes Festival (Festival Maroneias-Sapon)
events.when: annually from late June to September
events.blurb: The annual cultural festival of the Maroneia-Sapes Municipality runs across the summer with theatrical performances, concerts, open-air cinema screenings and local cultural events. It is organized by the municipality with support from the Ministry of Culture and the Region of East Macedonia and Thrace.

events.name: Feast of Saint Charalambos (Agios Charalambos)
events.blurb: Saint Charalambos is the patron saint of Maroneia, and his feast is marked on 10 February with a church liturgy and a procession of the town's miraculous icon of the saint.

events.name: Dekapentavgoustos (Dormition of the Virgin Mary) Festival in Akoumia
events.blurb: Akoumia, the traditional Cretan village nearest to Triopetra beach, keeps a lively atmosphere during summer and especially around the August 15th feast of the Dormition of the Virgin Mary, the major religious celebration of the Greek calendar.

events.name: Feast of the Transfiguration of the Savior, Akoumia
events.blurb: The Church of the Savior Christ (Sotiras Christos) at Akoumia is dedicated to the Transfiguration of the Savior, which is celebrated on 6 August.

events.name: Feast of Saint Onoufrios, Akoumia
events.blurb: The historic Saint Onoufrios chapel, set in a ravine of the Siderotas range above Akoumia near Triopetra, marks its feast day on 12 June, the commemoration of Saint Onuphrius.

events.name: Lixouri Carnival (Karnavali Lixouriou)
events.when: annually in the weeks before Clean Monday (Feb/Mar); 2026 grand parade 22 Feb 2026
events.blurb: Lixouri hosts one of Kefalonia's most famous carnivals with thematic groups and a grand parade. The 2026 season culminates in the main carnival parade on 22 February, the day before Clean Monday.

events.name: Feast of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary (Dekapentavgoustos)
events.blurb: On 15 August Lixouri marks the Feast of the Assumption with a church service followed by a lively panigiri featuring traditional Kefalonian music, dance and local food in the town. Village squares across Paliki hold their own celebrations on the eve.

events.name: Varkarola (Varkaroles) of Lixouri
events.blurb: Local fishing boats are decorated with colourful lights and parade past the Lixouri waterfront while singers perform traditional Kefalonian 'kantades' for spectators along the harbour.

events.name: Kefalonia Gym Festival
events.blurb: One of the largest 'Gymnastics for All' events in Greece and Europe, this four-day festival stages performances by athletic groups in different parts of Kefalonia, including Lixouri.

events.name: Mantzavinata Wine Festival
events.blurb: A traditional wine festival held each August in the village of Mantzavinata, roughly 2-4 km from Xi Beach, organized by the local cultural association in the former school courtyard. It celebrates the village's wine-making heritage with local wine, live music and dancing.

events.name: Lixouri Carnival (Apokries)
events.blurb: Kefalonia's largest and most famous carnival, held in the town of Lixouri (nearest town to Xi Beach) in the weeks before Orthodox Lent. Known for its satirical floats and big street parade, with the grand parade scheduled for 22 February 2026.

events.name: Lixouri Festival of Gastronomy & Wine
events.blurb: A festival held in Lixouri's main square featuring live cooking shows with local products, regional wine, music and dancing. It showcases Paliki peninsula gastronomy in the town nearest Xi Beach.

events.name: Agios Spyridon Feast (Patron Saint of Zacharo)
events.blurb: Zacharo celebrates its patron saint, Agios Spyridon, with a large procession at his hilltop church on 12 December.

events.name: Profitis Ilias Panigiri
events.blurb: A traditional local panigiri (saint's-day festival) honouring the Prophet Elijah (Profitis Ilias) is held in the Zacharo area each 20 July.

events.name: Zacharo Carnival (Apokries)
events.when: annually in late winter / early spring (Carnival season)
events.blurb: The town holds an annual Carnival celebration with parades and festivities during the pre-Lenten Apokries season.

events.name: Kakovatos Olive Festival (Elaias Paramythia)
events.blurb: An olive and local-produce festival held in Kakovatos near Zacharo, celebrating the area's olive cultivation and agricultural heritage.
